chunks: And in the narration of Zurarah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said:

"If you are behind an Imam, then do not recite anything in the first two, and listen silently to his recitation; and do not recite anything in the last two either, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to the believers,
"And when the Qur'an is recited"—meaning in the obligatory prayer behind the Imam—"then listen to it and remain silent, so that you may receive mercy."
So the last two are تابعًا to the first two.

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ: the last two rakʿahs of the prayer
key_terms.الْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ: the first two rakʿahs of the prayer

ai.seo_question: Should a follower recite behind the Imam in congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one praying behind an Imam in congregational salat: the follower should not recite in the first two rakʿahs and should listen silently. It extends the same ruling to the last two rakʿahs and supports it through the Qur'anic command to listen attentively when the Qur'an is recited.
